recordedBefore: release attempt 6, which is not yet declared. Set after attempts 4 (93.5%) and 5 (91.3%) were seen, so neither counts as passing it; it applies only to a fresh frozen run declared after this file.
status: Claude's call under Felipe's grant (2026-10-14: 'Have the freedom to have the highest precision you want, in a way that's good enough'). Reasons: commercial SAST precision is commonly reported at 18 to 36%, a 2025 open-source study found 180 of 2,116 flags real, tuned deployments reach 80 to 90%; at about 0.3 status-setting findings per repository, 95% is about one false Exposed in 60 audits. 97% stays reported as a stretch figure.
scope: Everything that sets a founder's status (Exposed or At risk): deterministic findings and the customer agent's admitted findings, as rendered, on a held-out set frozen before the change being measured. INFO facts are reported, not gated.

definitions.truePositive: both blind labelers agree the statement as written is accurate AND the issue is real against the deployed app
definitions.falsePositive: anything else, including partly accurate and contested (disagreement counts against us)
definitions.precision: TP / (TP + FP), with a one-sided 95% Clopper-Pearson lower bound
definitions.tieBreak: From release attempt 4 (Felipe authorized 2026-10-13, recorded before the attempt runs): when the two blind labelers split on a finding (one strict yes, one not), a third blind labeler answers it, and the finding is true when a majority of the three says accurate and real. Two labelers who agree are final. Attempts 1 to 3 are scored without it.

statusSetting.note: With 100 labeled findings, 95% observed means at most 5 false; the one-sided 95% lower bound is then about 89.7%.

statusCorrectness.note: Exposed or At risk is right when at least one issue setting it is a true positive; No open issues is reported with what was unread.

noFalseMissingCheck.note: Reported by the labelers' reasons; checked by hand at close until the harness counts it.

reportedNotGated: recall on named known vulnerabilities (misses listed by name)
